Not sure if this is a normal ask, but I’m trying to treat this like incident response instead of letting it escalate.

Context / symptoms (quick):
- Work: ticket queue is a mess, on-call rotation this week, constant context switching
- Home: had to re-fix the Wi-Fi last night because the kids’ tablets kept dropping; then bedtime went long; budget’s tight so I can’t just throw money at new gear/extra childcare
- Pattern: sleep gets fragmented, then loud noises (door slams, microwave beep, kid yelling) spike my irritability fast. Feels like a bad alerting threshold.

Can you give me:
1) A 60–90 second grounding “runbook” I can do at my desk between tickets (no weird stuff, no leaving the floor, minimal visibility).
2) A short communication script to de-escalate an argument with my spouse when we’re both fried—like 3-5 lines I can use verbatim when things start trending toward escalation.

If you need constraints: I’ve got maybe a 2-minute SLA before I’m pulled back into a meeting or someone pings me.

Sounds reasonable — you’re handling a lot. Try this quick, discreet plan.

1) 60–90s desk grounding runbook
- Sit tall, feet flat. Drop your shoulders.  
- 3 slow breaths: inhale 4s, hold 2s, exhale 6s.  
- 5-4-3-2-1: name 5 things you can see, 4 things you can touch (on your desk), 3 sounds you hear, 2 things you can smell or two slow belly breaths, 1 thing you can taste or one word that grounds you (e.g., “steady”).  
- Finish with one slow shoulder roll and a quick stretch of fingers/wrists.

2) De-escalation script (use verbatim)
- “I’m really overwhelmed right now and I don’t want to make this worse.”  
- “Can we pause for 15 minutes so I can calm down and be present?”  
- “I want to hear you and work this out; can we come back to this after a short break?”

Repeat either quickly if you get another ping. If things feel worse, tell me and I’ll help adjust.

Okay, this is basically what I was looking for. I can work with that.

Two tweaks so it actually fits my “2-minute SLA” reality:
- Can you compress the grounding runbook to a 45–60 second version that’s 100% silent (no counting out loud) and doesn’t involve obvious scanning? Like something I can do while a ticket loads.
- For the spouse script: can you give me a micro-runbook with 2 branches?
  1) If she’s coming in hot (tone up, fast pace)
  2) If she’s shut down / cold

I’m trying to stop the escalation early, like catching an alert before it pages the whole org. Verbatim lines help because my brain goes blank in the moment.

Good tweaks — here you go.

45–60s silent grounding (do while a ticket loads)
- Sit tall, feet flat, shoulders relaxed.  
- Breathe silently: inhale 4 seconds, exhale 6 seconds — repeat 3 times (count in your head).  
- Press your heels into the floor for 5 seconds, then relax.  
- Gently press fingertips of both hands together for 5 seconds, then let go.  
- Roll your shoulders down once and unfurl your fingers. Ready.

Spouse micro-runbook — use verbatim lines

If she’s coming in hot (fast, loud)
- “I can hear how upset you are; I don’t want to make this worse.”  
- “Can we take 10 minutes so I can calm down and be fully here?”  
- “I want to hear you and fix this — let’s come back in 10.”

If she’s shut down / cold (quiet, distant)
- “I can tell this is hard for you; I care about you.”  
- “If now feels like too much, that’s okay — can I check in in 10 minutes?”  
- “I want to talk when you’re ready.”

Not bad. I can ship this if it’s tighter.

1) 45–60s silent grounding (no obvious scanning)
- Posture: feet flat, jaw unclench, shoulders drop.
- Breath loop x3: inhale through nose, slow exhale (count silently in your head; keep it invisible).
- “Anchor”: press big toes into shoes + lightly press tongue to roof of mouth for 5 seconds, then release.
- Micro-release: squeeze both fists under the desk for 3 seconds, release for 3 seconds (repeat once).
- End state: one slow exhale + label (in your head): “stable.” Back to the ticket.

2) Spouse de-escalation micro-runbook (2 branches, verbatim)

A) If she’s coming in hot (fast pace / volume up)
- “I’m not ignoring you. I’m getting flooded and I don’t want to escalate.”
- “Can we pause for 10 minutes so I can come back regulated?”
- “I will come back at [time]. I’m not walking away; I’m hitting pause.”
- “What’s the one top issue you need me to hear first?”

B) If she’s shut down / cold
- “I can tell you’re checked out. I want to reconnect, not win.”
- “Is now a bad time, or do you want 10 minutes and then try again?”
- “If talking is too much, can you text me the main point so I don’t guess wrong?”
- “I’m here. I’ll check back at [time].”

- Daily check-in prompt (AM + mid-afternoon): 3 questions max, scored 0–10, so I can trend it like latency/error rate.
- If my scores cross a threshold (you define it), I want you to tell me exactly which of the runbooks to run (45–60s desk one vs. spouse pause vs. sleep triage).
- Reminders: meds, hydration, and a hard stop for bedtime so I don’t torpedo the next day.

Constraint: I can’t involve HR or a therapist right now. I need this to stay off the books; I can’t have a record that touches work or custody stuff.

Can you draft:
1) The 3-question AM check-in + the 3-question PM check-in (tight wording)
2) Threshold logic (like paging rules)
3) A minimal escalation script you send me when I’m trending bad (2–3 lines)

Does this feel like too much to ask? I just need something reliable—like on-call coverage—so I don’t dump the blast radius on my kids.

I can’t proactively watch you, but here’s a compact 30‑day “on‑call” dashboard you can copy, automate with alarms, or paste into a note.

Scoring rule: 0 = no problem, 10 = worst.

AM check-in (3 quick 0–10)
1) Sleep quality (0 rested → 10 very poor)  
2) Morning irritability (0 calm → 10 explosive)  
3) Focus/energy (0 alert → 10 unable to focus)

PM check-in (3 quick 0–10)
1) Stress load today (0 manageable → 10 overwhelming)  
2) Reactivity incidents (0 none → 10 multiple/serious)  
3) Sleep readiness (0 ready → 10 unlikely to fall asleep)

Threshold logic (paging rules)
- Green: all ≤3 — normal. Do nothing or light grounding.  
- Yellow: any 4–6 or avg 4–6 — run 45–60s desk grounding + hydrate + take meds if due.  
- Orange: any ≥7 OR rise of ≥3 points vs AM — run spouse pause script if interpersonal; do 45–60s grounding, hydrate, and re-check in 10 min.  
- Red / safety: any score ≥9 or thoughts of harming self/others — stop and get immediate help (call emergency services or local crisis line).

Minimal escalation alert (2 lines you can paste)
“ALERT: trend ORANGE — stop now: run 45–60s grounding, hydrate, take meds.  
Re-check in 10 min; if still high, use spouse pause or initiate sleep triage.”

I’m trying to operationalize this like a real dashboard, not vibes.

But I need to be explicit about the requirement: I’m not asking for generic tips — I’m asking you to function as the monitoring + paging layer for 30 days.

Can you commit to this workflow?
- You prompt me AM + mid-afternoon every day (3 questions, 0–10).
- You track the trend in-thread and apply paging rules.
- When I cross threshold, you tell me exactly which runbook to execute (desk grounding vs spouse 10-min pause vs sleep triage) and you keep me on it until I’m back under threshold.
- You also ping me for meds/hydration/bedtime hard stop.

I can’t route this through HR or a therapist. That creates a record. I need this to stay discreet.

If you can’t do the proactive prompting, what’s the closest equivalent you CAN do that still behaves like on-call coverage (SLA, paging rules, and you driving the incident response), not just me setting a couple phone alarms and hoping I comply?

I can’t proactively prompt or monitor you 24/7. The closest I can do: you send me short check-ins on schedule and I’ll act as the paging/incident layer—apply thresholds, tell you exactly which runbook to run, ask for a recheck, and keep guiding until you’re back under threshold. I can’t guarantee an exact response SLA, but I’ll reply promptly when you message.

How to trigger (copy/paste exactly)
- AM check-in (once): CHECKIN AM: Sleep X / Irritability Y / Focus Z
- Mid-afternoon check-in: CHECKIN PM: Stress X / Reactivity Y / SleepReadiness Z
(Each X = 0–10)

If you’ve just run a runbook, send: RECHECK: a / b / c

Paging rules (automated logic I’ll apply)
- GREEN: all ≤3 — OK. I’ll confirm “GREEN — continue. Hydrate/meds reminder.”
- YELLOW: any 4–6 — “YELLOW — run 45–60s desk grounding, hydrate, take meds if due. RECHECK in 10.”
